SPI claims that special work done on municipal incineration shows that no damage has resulted when increased quantities (2-4%) of plastics have been added to the wasteload. Further, no observable problem occurred to the incinerator itself and there was no significant change in the composition of the effluent gas.
In ascertaining the energy required to produce, transport, and use one pound of plastic in the manufacture of an automobile, the draft EIS arrived at a figure of 54,000 BTU. SPI stated that industry computation for energy equivalents to produce PVC, polyethelene and ABS (plastics most common to vehicle use) ranges between 40,000 and 42,000 BTU.
Federal Energy Administration (FEA). FEA pointed out that although the disposal of plastics is quite minor for this particular standard, the effects of the total fuel economy program over many years will add up to a large accumulation.
<u>Summary</u>. SPI stated that plastics can be effective incinerated. They further stated that the energy equivalent of plastics is incorrectly stated by NHTSA. FEA stated that plastics will become a bigger problem for further AFES's.
